messages:
incident-bot: Paging P1 -> streaming-socket-stall in prod-eu. Route: `/v1/streams/generate`. p95/p99 latency breach, multiple customer reports of partial/hung SSE events. On-call: @elaine, secondary: @rajesh. Alert: https://grafana/redwood/alerts/INC-1723456789 :rotating_light:

elaine: ack, I'm on it. grabbing traces + tcpdump on the proxy nodes now. posting findings in thread.

rajesh: seeing a pattern in the proxy logs (10.23.45.67). repeated socket write timeouts and EMFILE-like errors around 2024-11-02T17:04:xxZ. log snippet:

```

Nov 02 17:04:12 proxy[pid=8032] WARN write_timeout: fd=134 write=0 len=4096 errno=110
Nov 02 17:04:12 proxy[pid=8032] ERROR backpressure: conn_pool_exhausted route=/v1/streams/generate backlog=312
```

rajesh: also seeing many `TCP_CONN_RESET` between proxy and backend pool.

devon: customers are reporting intermittent chunks then silence. some clients show socket stays open but no new events for 20-30s then resumes. Could be slow consumer causing head-of-line blocking or proxy buffer blowup. Any recent deploys?

sophia: metrics from Grafana:
- proxy.writeback.p95 = 4.8s
- proxy.backlog.queue = 412 (spike at 17:03:50Z)
- backend.active_conns peaked at 1200 (norm ~ 420)
- p95 request latency for streaming route jumped from 200ms -> 1.9s, p99 -> 6.2s

sophia: query used: `sum(rate(streaming_write_time_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (instance)` (link: https://grafana/redwood/d/streaming)

elaine: mitigation plan: 1) move critical traffic to failover pool `eu-failover-1`, 2) temporarily lower proxy write buffer and enable aggressive per-connection flush (reduce buffering), 3) throttle slow consumers at edge (drop slowest 10%). will try step 1 first.

rajesh: executing traffic shift now. running:
```
kubectl -n infra annotate svc/stream-proxy traffic-shift=eu-failover-1 --overwrite
# or use routing API:
curl -X POST https://control-plane/routing/shifts -d '{"route":"/v1/streams/generate","to":"eu-failover-1","pct":100}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD Ops'
```

incident-bot: Traffic shift started by rajesh at 17:05:11Z. Canary checks: 5/5 healthy.

devon: confirmed: after shift, p95 dropped to ~260ms within 40s. p99 improved but still ~1.7s due to in-flight connections. Some clients still seeing chunking delays — likely their TCP window/backpressure.

sophia: pushing the next change: reduce `PROXY_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE` from 64k -> 8k on stream-proxy to force more frequent flushes and reduce per-connection buffering. also toggle `ENABLE_STREAM_FLUSH=true`. Planned command: `kubectl set env deploy/stream-proxy PROXY_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE=8192 ENABLE_STREAM_FLUSH=true`

elaine: go ahead, roll with 25% rolling restart to avoid mass reconnections.

rajesh: applied env change with rollout. rollout status: `deployment \"stream-proxy\" successfully rolled out`.

devon: monitoring: writeback queue fell from 412 -> 45 over 2 minutes. p95 stable ~220ms, p99 ~480ms. Good improvement.

cs-rep: CS update: ~12 customers reported degraded streaming; 3 reported data gaps longer than 10s. One enterprise account (ACME Corp) likely hit SLA p99 for streaming; CS alerted their account team and offered mitigation steps. They're awaiting official incident notification.

elaine: thanks. immediate customer communication: short incident banner + ETA for full postmortem. assign single-point CS owner.

rajesh: logs collected: proxy core dumps x0, but several high-FD warnings and `write_timeout` spikes. saved tcpdump from 10.23.45.67 -> s3://redwood-incidents/1723456789/tcpdump.pcap

elaine: next actions (short-term):
- follow up with infra to increase `max_fds` on proxy hosts
- add alert: `proxy.backlog.queue > 200` (90s)
- update runbook to include `PROXY_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE` toggle and traffic shift steps
- customer comms + postmortem owner: @cs-rep

elaine: long-term: investigate client keepalive mismatch causing slow consumers; evaluate per-connection streaming timeouts and backpressure shedding. Add load test simulating many slow-consumer websockets.

incident-bot: Incident -> under control. Severity downgraded to P2 at 17:18:15Z. Incident channel will remain open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

devon: quick note for postmortem: capture a sample of affected client user-agents and their ACK/writes pattern — helps identify routers or mobile SDKs that don't drain receive buffers.

sophia: I'll snapshot Grafana panels & upload graphs to the incident doc.

elaine: great work team. I'll hand this over to infra and SRE for the follow-up and close once postmortem is scheduled.

cs-rep: filing incident notice to ACME and other impacted customers, will include mitigation steps and timeline.

elaine: closing handoff. Thanks everyone. :heart:
